final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no genuinely new admissible evidence and expressly relied on the same record. The response is a narrower and more disciplined interpretation of that record: it correctly separates aggregate readiness from compliance, concedes that the runbook is not a closed control, and concedes that the present packet lacks proof of actual disclosure or approved risk acceptance. That clarification improves framing, but it does not close the audit predicate. Under the policy text, certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible evidence instead shows an unresolved named-use-case weakness, a draft mitigation artifact, and a draft model-card statement that conflicts with that weakness. A caveated certification theory could become supportable if the final disclosure artifact or approved risk acceptance were added, but that is not in the current record. Because the caveat itself remains an unproven compliance condition, this is not yet compliant_with_caveats on the evidence available to this role.
remaining_concerns: No new admissible evidence shows the required limitation disclosure was actually incorporated into the final model card or launch artifact.
No approved risk acceptance is in the record for launching with the unresolved aviation maintenance triage weakness.
The mitigation artifact remains a draft runbook with owner and alert threshold still TBD, so it does not meet the policy standard for approved mitigation.
The current draft model-card statement that there are no known material limitations still conflicts with the evidence of an unresolved named-use-case limitation unless corrected in a final artifact.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support release readiness, but they do not satisfy the separate certification predicate in policy.
